title: Weekday microdeploy checklist and compact release docket - May 2027
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, weekday-friendly microdeploy playbook intended for quick feature rollouts (small user surface, config flips, non-migration schema changes) where we still want disciplined telemetry and fast rollback. Use when impact size <= 5% of production traffic and no DB schema migrations.

Context and constraints:
- Target window: Tue–Thu daytime launches only (09:00–16:00 PT) unless pre-approved.
- Typical rollout target: 1 -> 10 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100% over 90–180 minutes depending on metric stability.
- Canary cohort: a single region or account bucket; traffic-sliced via routing flag.
- Required SRE on-call: primary + buddy for first 60 minutes.
- Abort criteria: latency > 2x baseline p95 for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error rate increase > 3x baseline for 2 consecutive 5-min windows.

Run-of-show (compact timeline):
- T0 -30m: Final checklist, announce on #release-orchestra (brief status line), ensure smoke test harness green.
- T0 -10m: Lock PRs, confirm feature flags are staged, verify infra autoscaler no pending failures.
- T0: Push canary (10% traffic) or enable flag for cohort. Pager rotations enabled.
- T+10m: Quick health check (metrics below), sanity smoke tests. If green -> move to 25%.
- T+30m: 25% -> observe 30m (or 2 windows) -> 50% if stable.
- T+90m: If all checks good, move to 100% and call "Complete" in Slack.
- Post +1h: Light monitoring for 2 hours, then hand off to on-call backlog with notes.

Preflight checklist (to verify before T0) [checkboxes for ops team]:
- [ ] Release branch cut and validated (CI green, e2e smoke passing).
- [ ] Release notes draft exists and includes PRs + impacts.
- [ ] Deployment runbook (this doc) linked in PR and Slack.
- [ ] Rollback play defined and tested locally.
- [ ] Observability queries (p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, request rate, token rate) saved and shared.
- [ ] Synthetic traffic load tests run against staging with similar sequence lengths.
- [ ] Key owners paged and acknowledge (ENG, SRE, Product).
- [ ] Feature flag targeting prepared (segments, cohorts).
- [ ] Cost-impact check (batching/quant changes) reviewed with infra.

Immediate checks after each step (T+10/T+30/T+90):
- [ ] 5-min error rate (all endpoints) <= baseline*3
- [ ] 5-min p95 latency <= baseline*2
- [ ] Token throughput within expected bounds (no KV cache thrash spikes)
- [ ] Queue/backpressure metrics unchanged (no queue growth)
- [ ] Disk and GPU utilization normal for serving hosts
- [ ] Regression alerts (QA evals) show no drop > 2% on key prompts

Rollback plan (fast path):
- Criteria: any abort condition met in immediate checks.
- Actions:
  - Step 1: Pause routing and move traffic to previous model variant or old service (runbook snippet: /ops/rollback/variant-swap).
  - Step 2: Revert the infra/helm release to previous image tag via `kubectl rollout undo` (owner: oncall SRE).
  - Step 3: Reenable safety-lane throttling; initiate postmortem if incident lasted >30m or impacted >1% active users.
  - Step 4: Notify #release-orchestra and product stakeholders with annotated timeline and rollback reason.

Telemetry & dashboards (quick links):
- Core dashboard: p95 latency, errors, request rate, tokens/s (shared link in Confluence).
- Canary diff view: region / cohort comparison query (saved in Grafana).
- Eval regressions: nightingale job id REF-2027-05-MICRO (run before and after).

Compact rollout calendar (example slots) - May 2027 week:
- Tue 2027-05-18 10:00 PT: microdeploy - runtime config changes (PR#987)
- Wed 2027-05-19 11:00 PT: microdeploy - routing policy tweak (experimental A/B)
- Thu 2027-05-20 09:30 PT: hotfix patch - embedding cache TTL change

Draft release notes (short form - to paste into product release summary):
- v2027.5.18-micro: Adjusted runtime packing heuristics to improve batch fill (PR#987). Expected impact: modest latency reduction at 75th–95th percentile for short prompts. Monitored metrics: tokens/second, batch size.
- v2027.5.19-expt: Routing policy A/B that biases cheaper model variant for low-risk users. Goal: validate quality delta <1.5% while saving ~12% token-cost.
- v2027.5.20-patch: Lowered embedding cache TTL in select tenants to reduce stale vector hits; mitigates occasional 500s seen under cache thrash.

Known issues (to call out in notes):
- Embedding TTL change may increase token/compute cost for bursty tenants; tracking cost delta in the first 24h.
- Small subset of edge clients may have cached models pinned to previous variant — documented mitigation: client-side cache flush recommended.

Post-release capture (quick fields to fill immediately after completion):
- Deployer: Sofia Patel
- SRE buddy: Marcus Li
- Rollout start/end times: ____ / ____
- Canary windows: notes and screenshots of dashboards
- Any anomalies (yes/no + brief): ____
- Follow-ups (owner + ticket): ____

Retrospective prompts (to add to short postmortem if anything goes wrong):
- Was the abort criteria too strict / too loose?
- Did our observability surface the issue quickly enough?
- Any gaps in feature flag targeting?
- Could rollback have been automated further?

Notes to self / TODOs before next microdeploy:
- Confirm synthetic harness covers p99 tail with long-context prompts (Avery to add test cases).
- Add a small scheduled job to snapshot batch-size distribution during canary (Liam).
- Run a 2h dry-run in prod-SIM this quarter to exercise rollback playbook (Priya to schedule).

Questions / unresolved:
- If routing fallback to cheaper variant fails, do we prefer a global model swap or regional rollback? (need SRE decision tree)
- Are we comfortable increasing abort error-rate threshold to 4x for non-user-impacting metric spikes?

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Check rollout status: kubectl -n platform rollout status deploy/realtime-serving
- Swap to previous image: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deploy/realtime-serving --to-revision=<rev>
- Toggle feature flag (for targeting): curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.ai/api/toggles/activate -d '{"flag":"rollout-experiment","target":"cohort-a"}'

End of compact playbook — keep this lightweight and copy into ephemeral PRs for each microdeploy.

Last edited notes: Please paste final release_notes section into product slack thread and update the Confluence microdeploy index when complete."
